title: Striped counter
prompt:
Implement a concurrent key -> count map.

  void increment(String key)   // add one to this key's count (a new key starts at 0)
  long get(String key)         // this key's count; 0 for a key nobody incremented

It has to stay exact with four threads incrementing eight shared keys at once -
no lost updates. Any of these earns full marks:
- ConcurrentHashMap<String, LongAdder> + computeIfAbsent
- ConcurrentHashMap<String, AtomicLong> + computeIfAbsent, or merge() on Long
- a plain HashMap with every method synchronized
A HashMap with an unsynchronized get-then-put does not: that read-modify-write
loses increments (and can corrupt the map outright).

Keep both signatures exactly as given: no `throws`, nothing `private`.
